result.looks_like: Per region: frag1 (L 0-22.6s) = backward spelled-out SPEECH (formants <8kHz). frag3 (22.68-24.15s) = dot-matrix BITMAP at 440Hz harmonics. frag4 carrier (tail 25.17-32.46s) = DSB-SC AMPLITUDE-MODULATED bursts, NOT a clean bitmap and NOT plain tones: each burst shows two sidebands with a notch at a ~7.6-8.0kHz suppressed carrier; down-shifting by ~7.75kHz (analytic * exp(-j2pi*fc*t)) recovers voiced/formant-like baseband filling 0-6kHz (formant glides visible) = frequency-SHIFTED SPEECH, likely spelled-out characters paralleling frag1. Per-burst spectral center varies widely (5.3-14.2kHz), i.e. the modulating content (or baseband frequency) differs per burst -- so the decoder must NOT assume one fixed demodulation; it should both (a) coherently demodulate DSB-SC per burst and inspect baseband audio/spectrogram, and (b) consider that the per-burst center/offset itself encodes the symbol (FSK-like).
